findings.reason: it should build the JT-60SA operator from the description (declaring the MMSYS channels as the conductors' drive) and reuse `assemble_pf_currents` unchanged, rather than adding a parallel placement step, which is the reuse map the plan's own §6 preamble asks for.
findings.text: the plan states "the only JT-60SA addition is the step that places the measured MMSYS coil currents on the operator's `G_pf` columns, because `assemble_pf_currents` reads MAST's raw amc channels"; the method is not MAST-bound — it reads `self.pf_amc_channels`, which `build_operator` populates from `geometry.conductors`' declared drive channel (`operator.py:337`), with the MAST label→amc table (`operator.py:240) only a fallback for geometry that declares none — so a JT-60SA operator built from the §4 description already places the currents and the proposed step duplicates it.

reuse_search-1.reason: Acted in plan v90: section 6 reuses ForwardOperator.assemble_pf_currents unchanged, with MMSYS channels declared as the coils' drive.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new behaviour hides behind small interfaces that carry real work: one binding slot carrying named-struct-entry selection that composes with rank/position (`imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:193` `_read_ids_path`), one converter entry point (`imas_ambix/data/selene_deck.py`), one exporter function (`imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py:349`), and extensions to owners (`StoreEngine.open`, `eddb.py`, `artifact_resolution` pins) rather than a spread of wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the sections name the owner each extends: `eddb.py` gains the grid writer beside `write_channel` (no second store), `gs/artifact_resolution.py` owns the machine-keyed pins, `gs/machine_selection.py`/`machine_identity.py` own selection, `spine_bench/shots.py` owns the shot set, `data/signal_map.py` and `tokamap_export._unit_factor` retain unit conversion, and `data/cocos_convention.py` plus `challenge/convention.py` are extended rather than forked. The reference-equilibrium read is the one place two shapes coexist (`challenge/loader.py` `EfitLabels` for the convention kernel, `worldmodel/equilibrium_labels.py` `EquilibriumGeometry` for the referee); those serve distinct consumers, so the plan's "one equilibrium has one shape" is scoped to §6 rather than a fork — noted, not a finding.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. Every section that adds surface carries its own accounting: §2's exporter "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §4's struct selector "widens one binding contract and retires nothing"; §5 "adds one data file and no public definition or refusal family"; §7's EQDB rung "adds one remote script and one fetch entry … retires nothing, because no equilibrium-database reader exists" and "adds two record fields and retires nothing".
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan asserts one JT-60SA-specific coil-current placement step onto the operator's `G_pf` columns, but `ForwardOperator.assemble_pf_currents` is already description-driven through `pf_amc_channels`, which `build_operator` fills from each conductor's declared drive channel (`imas_ambix/gs/operator.py:337`), not from MAST constants.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — where the plan adds a layer it names why the underlying machinery cannot carry it: the tokamap exporter is kept out of the loaders because they read the ambix schema and must not learn tokamap's (`imas_ambix/data/tokamap_export.py` vs `machine_map.py`), the EQDB rung reuses `SshTransport` (`imas_ambix/data/eddb_remote.py`) rather than a second transport, and the SELENE reference enters `read_efit_geometry(loader=...)` (`imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py:120`) rather than a parallel comparator.
